nodes.name: Model
nodes.definition: A simplified representation of some part of reality, chosen to make it graspable and to predict it.

nodes.name: Representation
nodes.definition: Something that stands in for a set of experiences or objects so they can be reasoned about as one thing.

nodes.name: Clustering
nodes.definition: Grouping unlabeled data points so that points in the same group are more similar to each other than to points in other groups.

nodes.name: Abstraction
nodes.definition: Deliberately ignoring details so that many different things can be treated as one; every model is a choice of what to ignore.

nodes.name: Extrapolation
nodes.definition: Using a pattern compressed from past observations to predict cases beyond those observations.

nodes.name: Induction
nodes.definition: Inferring a general rule from repeated specific observations, such as concluding the sun will rise because it always has.

nodes.name: Domain of validity
nodes.definition: The range of conditions under which a model gives useful predictions, beyond which it breaks down.

nodes.name: Falsification
nodes.definition: Testing a model by actively trying to prove it wrong, since a model can never be proven right.

nodes.name: Model refinement
nodes.definition: Replacing a working model with a deeper one that explains it and extends further, as kinetic theory did for temperature.

nodes.name: Function approximation
nodes.definition: Finding a function F that maps inputs x to outputs y from examples, the common shape of most machine learning tasks.
previewed_in: Say Exactly What You Mean: A First Look at Python

nodes.name: Supervised learning
nodes.definition: Learning a mapping from inputs to outputs using examples where the correct output is given.

nodes.name: Unsupervised learning
nodes.definition: Finding structure in data that comes without labels, such as clusters or low-dimensional directions.

nodes.name: Program
nodes.definition: A precise sequence of instructions that a computer follows exactly, with no common sense to fill gaps.

nodes.definition: A symbol such as +, /, ** or % that computes a number from other numbers in code.

nodes.name: Assignment

nodes.name: Data type
nodes.definition: The kind of a value (number, text, boolean) that determines what operations on it mean.

nodes.name: List
nodes.definition: An ordered collection of values in a program, accessed by position.

nodes.name: Indexing

nodes.name: Conditional
nodes.definition: An if/else statement that runs different code depending on whether a condition is true.

nodes.name: Loop
nodes.definition: A statement that repeats a block of code for each item or until a stopping rule is met.

nodes.name: Execution trace
nodes.definition: Following a program line by line while tracking what value each name holds, to see what the computer actually does.

nodes.name: Function
nodes.definition: A named, reusable rule that takes inputs and returns an output, both in mathematics and as a recipe in code.

nodes.name: Dictionary
nodes.definition: A container that maps keys to values, so a value is found by its key rather than by its position.

lesson.title: Dictionary

nodes.name: Debugging
nodes.definition: Finding and fixing errors in a program, starting by reading what the error message says.

nodes.name: Symbolic AI
nodes.definition: The early approach to artificial intelligence that hand-codes rules and searches over symbols, rather than learning from data.

nodes.name: Machine learning
nodes.definition: Building systems that learn rules or patterns from data instead of having them programmed by hand.

nodes.name: Moore's law
nodes.definition: The observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years.

nodes.name: Compute scaling
nodes.definition: The growth by many orders of magnitude of the computation used to train AI systems, a main driver of recent progress.

nodes.name: Log scale
nodes.definition: A plot axis where equal distances mean equal ratios, used when values span many orders of magnitude.

lesson.title: Or Just Ask For the Plot

nodes.name: Curve fitting
nodes.definition: Choosing a function whose curve passes close to a set of data points.

lesson.title: A Lot of It Is Curve Fitting

nodes.name: Graph
nodes.definition: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to represent relationships such as social networks, maps or molecules.

nodes.name: Data representation
nodes.definition: The way something recorded from the world, like sound, images or text, is turned into numbers a machine can process.

nodes.name: Tabular data
nodes.definition: Data arranged as a table, where each row is an example and each column is a measured quantity.

nodes.name: Time series
nodes.definition: A sequence of measurements indexed by time, such as a stock price recorded each day.

nodes.name: Audio signal
nodes.definition: Sound recorded as an array of air-pressure samples taken many thousands of times per second.

nodes.name: Spectrogram
nodes.definition: A picture of a sound showing how much energy each frequency has over time, built from short-time Fourier transforms.

lesson.title: From a Wave to a Picture

previewed_in: Time Series Analysis: Starting from Data

nodes.name: Fourier transform
nodes.definition: A transformation that rewrites a signal as a sum of sinusoids, revealing which frequencies it contains.

lesson.title: From a Wave to a Picture

nodes.name: Image representation
nodes.definition: An image stored as a grid of pixel values, of shape height by width by number of channels.

nodes.name: Color channel
nodes.definition: One of the red, green or blue grids of intensities that together make up a colour image.

nodes.name: Tensor
nodes.definition: A multi-dimensional array of numbers, such as a video of shape time by height by width by channels.

nodes.name: Word embedding
nodes.definition: A dense vector for each word, learned so that directions and distances between vectors carry meaning.

nodes.name: Adjacency matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix whose entry (i, j) is 1 when node i connects to node j, representing a graph as numbers.

nodes.name: Modeling, learning, inference
nodes.definition: The three pillars of AI: build a simplified model, estimate its parameters from data, then use it to answer questions.

lesson.title: The Three Pillars of Artificial Intelligence

nodes.name: Classification
nodes.definition: Predicting a discrete label, such as fraud or not fraud, from an input.

nodes.name: Regression
nodes.definition: Predicting a continuous numerical value, such as a house price, from an input.

nodes.name: Structured prediction
nodes.definition: Predicting an output with internal structure, such as a sentence or a parse tree, rather than a single label or number.

nodes.name: Histogram
nodes.definition: A bar chart of how many data samples fall into each range of values.

nodes.name: Probability density function
nodes.definition: A curve describing how likely a continuous variable is to take values near each point; a model of the data, unlike the histogram.

nodes.name: Notation and code
nodes.definition: Every mathematical idea in the course is written two ways, as compact notation and as runnable code, and each translates directly into the other.

lesson.title: Every Idea, Written Twice
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Iteration
nodes.definition: Repeating one update step in a loop, so that a model like next year's population from this year's steps forward through time.

lesson.title: The loop that predicts the future
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Vectors
nodes.definition: An ordered list of numbers, pictured as an arrow with direction and length; in machine learning one example, one row of data, is a vector.

lesson.title: Vectors
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Inner product
nodes.definition: The sum of elementwise products of two vectors, also called the dot product; the single most common operation in machine learning.

lesson.title: Vector Operations
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Norm
nodes.definition: A measure of a vector's length, such as the L2 (Euclidean), L1 (sum of absolute values), or max norm; distances between examples are norms of differences.

lesson.title: How Long, How Far, How Similar
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Cosine similarity
nodes.definition: The cosine of the angle between two vectors, their dot product divided by both lengths, measuring how similar their directions are regardless of size.

lesson.title: How Long, How Far, How Similar
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Matrix
nodes.definition: A rectangular array of numbers with rows and columns; it can hold a whole dataset or act as a linear transformation of vectors.

lesson.title: Matrices
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Matrix multiplication
nodes.definition: Combining two matrices so each output entry is a row-by-column dot product; in NumPy it is A @ B, not the elementwise A * B.

lesson.title: Matrices in NumPy
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Linear transformation
nodes.definition: A map that moves space while keeping lines straight and the origin fixed; a matrix's columns record where the basis vectors land.

lesson.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Determinant
nodes.definition: The factor by which a matrix scales area or volume; a determinant of zero means the matrix flattens space and cannot be inverted.

lesson.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Eigenvector
nodes.definition: A direction that a matrix only stretches or shrinks without turning; the stretch factor is its eigenvalue.

lesson.title: A matrix is a machine that moves space
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Composition of transformations
nodes.definition: Applying one linear transformation after another, which equals multiplying their matrices; order matters, so RS generally differs from SR.

lesson.title: Two machines in a row are one machine
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Column space
nodes.definition: The set of all outputs Ax, read as weighted sums of the columns of A, where x supplies the weights.

lesson.title: Two Ways to Read Ax
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Span
nodes.definition: Everything you can build from a set of vectors by scaling and adding them together.

lesson.title: Span, Independence, Rank
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Rank
nodes.definition: The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, which is the dimension of the space its outputs can reach.

lesson.title: Span, Independence, Rank
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Matrix inverse
nodes.definition: The matrix that undoes A, so multiplying them gives the identity; it solves the linear system Ax = b when it exists.

lesson.title: Inverse, Determinant, and When Things Break
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Condition number
nodes.definition: A measure of how much a matrix amplifies small errors when inverted; nearly duplicate columns make it huge and the solution unreliable.

lesson.title: When the Inverse Quietly Lies
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Derivative
nodes.definition: The slope of a curve at a point, what the curve looks like up close: how fast the output changes as the input nudges.

lesson.title: A derivative is what a curve looks like up close
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Integral
nodes.definition: The accumulated total of a rate, the area under its curve; integration and differentiation undo each other.

lesson.title: A rate and its total
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Gradient
nodes.definition: The vector of partial derivatives of a function with respect to each parameter, pointing in the direction of steepest increase.

lesson.title: The Calculus You Actually Need
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Normal equations
nodes.definition: The linear system obtained by setting the least-squares gradient to zero, whose solution gives the best-fit parameters in closed form.

lesson.title: The One Gradient You Will Use All Semester
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Projection
nodes.definition: The closest point to a vector within a subspace; least squares projects the targets onto the space spanned by the feature columns.

lesson.title: Least Squares Is a Projection
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Chain rule
nodes.definition: The rule that the derivative of a composition is the product of the derivatives of its parts, which is how networks compute gradients.

lesson.title: The chain rule, as a picture
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Backpropagation
nodes.definition: Computing all gradients of a network efficiently by applying the chain rule backward from the loss through each operation.

lesson.title: The chain rule, as a picture
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Variable aliasing
nodes.definition: A Python variable is a label on an object, not a box, so two names can share one object and a change through either shows in both.

lesson.title: A variable is a label, not a box
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Broadcasting
nodes.definition: NumPy's rule for combining arrays of different shapes by stretching size-one dimensions, a convenience that also causes silent shape bugs.

lesson.title: Broadcasting, and the Bug It Causes
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Vectorization
nodes.definition: Replacing explicit Python loops with whole-array operations, which run in optimized compiled code and are often hundreds of times faster.

lesson.title: Avoid Loops if You Can! Vectorize.
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: DataFrame
nodes.definition: A pandas table of labeled columns used to read, inspect, summarize, and clean a dataset before turning it into numeric arrays.

lesson.title: Reading and Exploring Data
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Design matrix
nodes.definition: The data matrix with one row per example and one column per feature, with the target held in a separate vector.

lesson.title: The Design Matrix
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Correlation
nodes.definition: A number between minus one and one measuring how linearly two variables move together, the dot product of their standardized columns divided by their count.

lesson.title: Statistics Is Linear Algebra
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Missing variable (Simpson's paradox)
nodes.definition: A trend in pooled data can reverse within groups when a hidden variable, such as species, drives both measurements.

lesson.title: The Same Data, Two Answers
lesson.deck_title: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.definition: A table of examples and measurements that you can visualize, summarize, clean, and use to make predictions.

nodes.name: Feature
nodes.definition: An input variable given to the model, such as a house's size, bedrooms, or age.

nodes.name: Target
nodes.definition: The output variable the model is trying to predict, also called the label, such as a house's price.

nodes.name: Training example
nodes.definition: One input and output pair from the data, indexed by i, used to fit the model.
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets

nodes.name: Hypothesis
nodes.definition: The function a learning algorithm chooses to map inputs to predicted outputs.

nodes.name: Parameters
nodes.definition: The numbers, often called theta, that select one specific function from within the chosen model class and are adjusted by training.

nodes.name: Model class
nodes.definition: The family of candidate functions a learner searches over, such as linear, polynomial, or neural network models.

nodes.name: Linear model
nodes.definition: A prediction that is a weighted sum of the features plus an intercept, written as a single inner product of parameters and inputs.
previewed_in: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Intercept
nodes.definition: The constant term of a linear model, handled by adding a feature that is always one; it is the prediction when all features are zero.

nodes.name: Residual
nodes.definition: The difference between a model's prediction and the actual target for one example.

nodes.name: Cost function
nodes.definition: A single number measuring how badly the model fits the data, such as half the sum of squared residuals, which training tries to minimize.

nodes.name: Loss landscape
nodes.definition: The surface formed by the cost at every possible parameter setting; its lowest point is the best fit.

nodes.name: Gradient descent
nodes.definition: An optimization method that repeatedly steps the parameters a small amount opposite the gradient, walking downhill on the cost.
previewed_in: Math and Python: Your Computational Toolkit

nodes.name: Learning rate
nodes.definition: The step size in gradient descent; too small is slow, too large overshoots and can diverge.

nodes.name: LMS update rule
nodes.definition: The least-mean-squares gradient step for linear regression, which moves each parameter in proportion to the prediction error times its feature.

nodes.name: Stochastic gradient descent
nodes.definition: Gradient descent that updates the parameters using one randomly chosen example (or small batch) per step, giving a faster but noisier path.

nodes.name: Centering features
nodes.definition: Subtracting a feature's mean so the intercept describes a typical example, which decouples slope and intercept and speeds up gradient descent.

lesson.title: Why we measure from the average house

nodes.name: Multiple regression
nodes.definition: Linear regression with several features at once, where each coefficient's value depends on which other features are included.

nodes.name: Holding other variables fixed
nodes.definition: A regression coefficient is the change in prediction per unit of its feature with every other feature held fixed, so it depends on the company it keeps.

lesson.title: θj answers one question at a time

nodes.name: Gaussian noise model
nodes.definition: The assumption that each target equals the model's prediction plus independent, normally distributed noise with mean zero.

lesson.title: Why Least Squares? A Probabilistic View

nodes.name: Likelihood
nodes.definition: The probability of the observed data viewed as a function of the parameters; for independent examples it is a product over them.

nodes.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
nodes.definition: Choosing parameters that make the observed data most probable; with Gaussian noise this is exactly least squares.

nodes.name: Outlier
nodes.definition: An unusual data point far from the pattern; squared error lets it pull the fit strongly toward itself.

nodes.name: Absolute error (L1 loss)
nodes.definition: A cost that sums absolute residuals instead of squared ones, which corresponds to Laplacian noise and is less sensitive to outliers.

nodes.name: k-nearest neighbours
nodes.definition: Predicting the output for a new input by averaging the outputs of the k training examples closest to it.

lesson.title: Given a new input, what’s the output?

nodes.name: Choosing the hypothesis
nodes.definition: The same data admits many fitting functions, so deciding which family of functions to use is a central modeling choice.

lesson.title: How do you choose the hypothesis?

nodes.name: Feature map
nodes.definition: A transformation that builds new features from raw inputs, such as Galton's mid-parent height or polynomial powers of x, before fitting a model.

nodes.name: Regression to the mean
nodes.definition: Galton's finding that children of unusually tall or short parents tend to be closer to average, which gave regression its name.

nodes.name: R squared
nodes.definition: The fraction of the target's variance explained by a fit: one minus residual variation over total variation.

lesson.title: A Fifth of the Variance, and a Whole Discipline

nodes.name: Overfitting
nodes.definition: When a model is too flexible and fits noise in the training data, giving low training error but poor performance on new data (high variance).

lesson.title: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)

nodes.name: Underfitting
nodes.definition: When a model is too simple to capture the real pattern, giving high error even on the training data (high bias).

lesson.title: How to choose φ(x)? How to optimize over φ(x)

nodes.name: Generalization
nodes.definition: A model's ability to perform well on new, unseen data, which is the real goal of machine learning.

lesson.title: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?

nodes.name: Test set
nodes.definition: Data held out from training and used once at the end to estimate how well the model generalizes.
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets

lesson.title: How can we tell if φ(·) is good?

nodes.name: Bias-variance trade-off
nodes.definition: As model complexity grows, error from too-simple assumptions (bias) falls while error from sensitivity to the particular data (variance) rises.

nodes.name: Hyperparameter
nodes.definition: A setting chosen outside the training loop, such as the number of epochs, the step size, or the feature map.

nodes.name: Validation set
nodes.definition: Held-out data used during development to compare models and tune hyperparameters, kept separate from the final test set.
nodes.wiki: Training, validation, and test data sets

lesson.title: Optimize over φ and other hyperparameters

nodes.name: Cross-validation
nodes.definition: Splitting data into folds and letting each fold take a turn as the validation set, averaging the results for a more reliable estimate.

lesson.title: Cross validation: every house takes a turn being new

nodes.name: Regularization
nodes.definition: Adding a penalty on parameter size to the cost, weighted by lambda, to shrink the hypothesis class and reduce overfitting.

nodes.name: L2 regularization
nodes.definition: A penalty on the squared size of the parameters (ridge) that shrinks all coefficients smoothly toward zero.

nodes.name: L1 regularization
nodes.definition: A penalty on the sum of absolute parameter values (lasso) that tends to drive some coefficients exactly to zero.

nodes.name: Sigmoid
nodes.definition: The logistic function 1/(1+e^-z), which squashes any real score into a probability between 0 and 1.

lesson.title: What if y is a label?

nodes.name: Logistic regression
nodes.definition: A classifier that passes a linear score through the sigmoid function to output the probability that the label is one.

lesson.title: What if y is a label?

nodes.name: Negative log-likelihood
nodes.definition: The negative logarithm of the likelihood, averaged over examples, used as a loss to minimise.

nodes.name: Convexity
nodes.definition: A property of a function shaped like a bowl, so that any local minimum is the global minimum.

nodes.name: Cross-entropy loss
nodes.definition: The loss for predicted probabilities that is near zero when confident and right and grows without bound when confident and wrong.

nodes.name: Decision boundary
nodes.definition: The surface in input space where a classifier switches its prediction from one class to another.

nodes.name: Margin
nodes.definition: The signed distance of a point from the decision boundary, positive when it is classified correctly.

nodes.name: Confusion matrix
nodes.definition: A table counting true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives of a classifier.

lesson.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?

nodes.name: Precision and recall
nodes.definition: Precision is the fraction of flagged cases that are real; recall is the fraction of real cases that were flagged.

lesson.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?

nodes.name: Accuracy
nodes.definition: The fraction of all predictions that are correct, which can mislead when classes are imbalanced.

lesson.title: Step 4: Test. But Accuracy of What?

nodes.name: F1 score
nodes.definition: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number that is low if either one is low.

lesson.title: The Same Four Numbers on One Screening

nodes.name: Class imbalance
nodes.definition: When one class is much rarer than the others, so that always predicting the majority class looks accurate.

nodes.name: Classification threshold
nodes.definition: The probability cutoff above which a classifier predicts the positive class, chosen after training to trade precision against recall.

nodes.name: Multiclass classification
nodes.definition: Classification where the label can take one of more than two values.

nodes.name: One-vs-all
nodes.definition: Handling many classes by training one binary classifier per class against all the others.

lesson.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?Note: this slide explains the intuition. Softmax regression is not exactly equivalent to a combination of one-vs-all classifiers.

nodes.name: Softmax
nodes.definition: A function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities by exponentiating and normalising them.

lesson.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?

nodes.name: Softmax regression
nodes.definition: The generalisation of logistic regression to many classes, with one linear score per class passed through softmax.

lesson.title: How to turn scores into probabilities?

nodes.name: Logit
nodes.definition: The raw score of a class before it is turned into a probability by a sigmoid or softmax.

nodes.name: Bernoulli distribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of a single yes or no outcome, equal to one with probability p and zero with probability one minus p.

nodes.name: Exponential family
nodes.definition: A broad class of distributions, including Gaussian, Bernoulli, and Poisson, sharing one form that yields the same learning update rule.

nodes.name: Natural parameter
nodes.definition: The parameter eta of an exponential-family distribution that multiplies the outcome inside the exponential; in a GLM it equals the linear score of the inputs.

nodes.name: Log partition function
nodes.definition: The term in an exponential-family distribution that normalizes probabilities to sum to one; its derivatives give the mean and variance.

nodes.name: Poisson distribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of the number of independent events in a fixed window, such as earthquakes in a decade, governed by an average rate.

nodes.name: Poisson regression
nodes.definition: A generalized linear model for count data where the logarithm of the expected count is linear in the features.

lesson.title: How many earthquakes of each size?

nodes.name: Generalized linear model
nodes.definition: A model that passes a linear score of the inputs through a response function matched to an exponential-family output, with the same training loop.

nodes.name: Link function
nodes.definition: The function connecting a GLM's expected output to its linear score; its inverse, the response function, turns the score into a prediction.

nodes.name: One-hot encoding
nodes.definition: Representing each item of a fixed vocabulary as a vector of zeros with a single one in its own position.

nodes.name: Bag of words
nodes.definition: Representing a document by which vocabulary words it contains, ignoring their order.
previewed_in: Say Exactly What You Mean: A First Look at Python

nodes.name: Class-conditional probability
nodes.definition: The probability of a feature given the class label, such as how often the word free appears in spam.

nodes.name: Naive Bayes assumption
nodes.definition: The simplifying assumption that features are conditionally independent given the label, so a message's probability is a product over its words.

nodes.name: Bayes' rule
nodes.definition: A formula that reverses conditional probabilities, getting the probability of a label given the data from the probability of the data given the label and the prior.

nodes.name: Prior
nodes.definition: The probability of a class before seeing any features, such as how common spam is overall.

nodes.name: Naive Bayes classifier
nodes.definition: A classifier that estimates class priors and per-feature class-conditional probabilities by counting, then combines them with Bayes' rule.

nodes.name: Laplace smoothing
nodes.definition: Adding a small count to every word and class so that an unseen word does not get probability zero and wipe out the whole product.

nodes.name: Event model
nodes.definition: The assumed story of how a message is generated, either a coin flip per vocabulary word (multivariate Bernoulli) or words drawn one at a time (multinomial).

lesson.title: Two ways to generate an email

nodes.name: Generative model
nodes.definition: A model that learns how each class's data is distributed, plus the class priors, then classifies with Bayes' rule and can generate new examples.

nodes.name: Discriminative model
nodes.definition: A model that learns the probability of the label given the input directly, drawing the decision boundary without modeling the inputs.

nodes.name: Multivariate Gaussian
nodes.definition: The bell-shaped distribution over vectors, described by a mean vector and a covariance matrix that sets its spreads and correlations.

nodes.name: Covariance matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix whose diagonal holds each variable's variance and whose off-diagonal entries measure how pairs of variables vary together.

nodes.name: Gaussian discriminant analysis
nodes.definition: A generative classifier that models each class's features as a multivariate Gaussian and classifies new points using Bayes' rule.

nodes.name: Language model
nodes.definition: A model that assigns probabilities to text by predicting each next word from the words before it.

nodes.definition: The largest absolute value among a matrix's eigenvalues, which sets whether repeated multiplication by it grows or shrinks vectors.

nodes.name: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
nodes.definition: A recurrent network whose gates control what a cell state forgets, stores and outputs, letting it keep information over long sequences.

nodes.name: Reservoir Computing
nodes.definition: Using a fixed, randomly connected recurrent network as a dynamical reservoir and training only a linear readout from its states.

nodes.name: Echo State Property
nodes.definition: The requirement that a reservoir's state depends on its input history and forgets its initial condition over time.

nodes.name: Physical Reservoir Computing
nodes.definition: Using a real physical system with nonlinear, fading-memory dynamics, such as optics or mechanics, as the reservoir of a reservoir computer.

nodes.name: Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Equation
nodes.definition: A fourth-order nonlinear PDE from flame fronts and chemical oscillations that is a standard test case for spatiotemporal chaos.

nodes.name: Spatiotemporal Chaos
nodes.definition: Chaotic behaviour that is irregular in both space and time, with sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

nodes.name: Lyapunov Time
nodes.definition: The characteristic time over which small errors in a chaotic system grow by a factor of e, setting the horizon of useful prediction.

nodes.name: Symbolic regression
nodes.definition: Searching over mathematical expressions to find a formula that fits data, without fixing the candidate terms in advance.

nodes.name: Expression Tree
nodes.definition: A tree representation of a formula in which internal nodes are operators and leaves are variables or constants.

nodes.name: Genetic Programming
nodes.definition: An evolutionary search that improves a population of programs or expression trees through selection, crossover and mutation.

nodes.name: Fitness Function
nodes.definition: The score an evolutionary algorithm uses to rank candidates, often fit error plus a penalty for complexity.

nodes.name: Selection
nodes.definition: The step of an evolutionary algorithm that chooses which candidates reproduce, favouring those with better fitness.

nodes.name: Crossover
nodes.definition: Creating offspring in an evolutionary algorithm by combining parts of two parents, such as swapping subtrees.

nodes.name: Mutation
nodes.definition: A random change to a candidate in an evolutionary algorithm, which introduces new material into the population.

nodes.name: Kepler's Third Law
nodes.definition: The law that a planet's orbital period squared is proportional to its orbital distance cubed, divided by the star's mass.

lesson.title: Now Do It On Something Real

nodes.name: Power Law
nodes.definition: A relationship of the form y = C x^a, which appears as a straight line on a log-log plot.

lesson.title: A Straight Line Where You Did Not Expect One

nodes.name: Pareto Front
nodes.definition: The set of candidates that no other candidate beats on every objective at once, such as accuracy and simplicity.

nodes.name: PySR
nodes.definition: A high-performance open-source library for symbolic regression using parallel evolving populations.

nodes.name: Bloat
nodes.definition: The tendency of evolved expression trees to grow larger without improving their fitness.

nodes.name: Boundary Condition
nodes.definition: A constraint on a differential equation's solution at the edges of its domain or at the initial time.

lesson.title: The Problem We Want to Solve

nodes.name: Basis Expansion
nodes.definition: Writing an unknown function as a weighted sum of fixed known functions such as sines or polynomials.

nodes.name: PDE Residual
nodes.definition: What remains when a candidate solution is substituted into a differential equation; it is zero everywhere for an exact solution.

nodes.name: Collocation Method
nodes.definition: Finding an approximate solution of a differential equation by making its residual small at a chosen set of points.

nodes.name: Physics-informed neural network
nodes.definition: A neural network trained so that its output satisfies a differential equation, by adding the equation residual to the loss.

nodes.name: Automatic Differentiation
nodes.definition: Computing exact derivatives of a program by applying the chain rule through its computation graph.

nodes.name: Physics-Informed Loss
nodes.definition: A loss that adds weighted terms for data fit, PDE residual and boundary conditions so one optimisation respects both data and physics.

nodes.name: Mesh-Free Method
nodes.definition: A numerical method that evaluates the solution at scattered points without building a mesh or grid.

nodes.name: Forward Problem
nodes.definition: Computing a system's solution when the governing equation and all its parameters are known.

lesson.title: Forward Problem: Solving a Known PDE

nodes.name: Loss Balancing
nodes.definition: Choosing or adapting the weights of different loss terms so that none dominates training.

nodes.name: Spectral Bias
nodes.definition: The tendency of neural networks to learn low-frequency components of a function before high-frequency ones.

nodes.name: Fourier Features
nodes.definition: Mapping inputs through sines and cosines of random frequencies before a network so it can represent high-frequency detail.

nodes.name: Operator
nodes.definition: A map that takes a function as input and returns another function.

nodes.name: Discretization Invariance
nodes.definition: The property that a learned model works on input and output grids of any resolution without retraining.

nodes.name: Universal Approximation for Operators
nodes.definition: The theorem that a suitable neural network can approximate any continuous nonlinear operator between function spaces.

nodes.name: Neural Operator
nodes.definition: A neural network that maps whole input functions to output functions, such as initial conditions to PDE solutions.

nodes.name: Solution Operator
nodes.definition: The map that takes a PDE's input data, such as an initial condition or forcing, to its solution.

nodes.name: Modal Decomposition
nodes.definition: Writing a field as a sum of spatial modes weighted by time-dependent coefficients.

nodes.name: DeepONet
nodes.definition: A neural operator that combines a branch network encoding the input function with a trunk network encoding the query point by a dot product.

nodes.name: Green's Function
nodes.definition: The response of a linear differential equation to a point impulse, from which any solution is built by integrating against the forcing.

nodes.name: Integral Kernel Layer
nodes.definition: A neural network layer that transforms a function by integrating it against a learned kernel, generalising a weight matrix to functions.

lesson.title: From Green's Functions to Neural Operator Layers

nodes.name: Fourier Neural Operator
nodes.definition: A neural operator whose layers multiply learned weights on a truncated set of Fourier modes, acting as a learned global convolution.

nodes.name: Self-Supervised Learning
nodes.definition: Learning from unlabeled data by predicting part of the data from other parts, so the data supplies its own labels.

nodes.name: Next-Token Prediction
nodes.definition: The training objective of predicting each token in a sequence from the tokens before it.

nodes.name: Pretraining
nodes.definition: The first, large-scale training stage of a model on broad unlabeled data before it is adapted to specific tasks.

nodes.name: Foundation Model
nodes.definition: A large model pretrained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks.

nodes.name: Transformer
nodes.definition: A neural network architecture built from stacked attention layers that processes a whole sequence at once rather than step by step.

nodes.name: Scaling Law
nodes.definition: An empirical power-law relation showing how model loss falls as compute, data, or parameters grow.

nodes.name: Fine-Tuning
nodes.definition: Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its behavior.

nodes.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

nodes.name: In-Context Learning

nodes.name: Emergent Capability
nodes.definition: An ability that appears in large models but seems absent in smaller ones, sometimes argued to be a measurement artifact.

nodes.name: Protein Structure Prediction

nodes.name: Protein Language Model
nodes.definition: A language model trained on protein sequences, treating amino acids as tokens, used to predict or design proteins.

nodes.name: AI Weather Forecasting
nodes.definition: Learned models such as GraphCast and GenCast that predict global weather from reanalysis data, rivaling numerical forecasts.

nodes.name: Evolutionary Search
nodes.definition: An optimization loop that proposes candidates, scores them with an evaluator, and keeps and mutates the best ones.

nodes.name: AI Agent
nodes.definition: A system in which a language model plans, chooses tools, executes actions, and iterates toward a goal using memory.

nodes.name: Tool Use
nodes.definition: A language model calling external functions such as code, search, or simulators through structured descriptions of their inputs.

nodes.name: ReAct Loop
nodes.definition: An agent loop that interleaves reasoning steps with actions and observations until a task is done.

nodes.name: Coding Agent
nodes.definition: An AI agent whose tools read, edit, search, and run code in a software project.

nodes.name: Prompt Engineering
nodes.definition: Designing the instructions, tools, and constraints given to a language model to shape its behavior.

nodes.name: Science Agent
nodes.definition: An AI agent whose tools are scientific operations such as data analysis, simulation, literature search, and lab experiments.

nodes.name: Autonomous Discovery
nodes.definition: Scientific discovery in which AI systems generate hypotheses, design and run experiments, and analyze results with little human input.

nodes.name: Multi-Agent System
nodes.definition: A system in which several AI agents with different roles cooperate on a task.

nodes.name: Scientific Method
nodes.definition: The cycle of observing, hypothesizing, experimenting, analyzing, and revising that produces scientific knowledge.

nodes.name: Hallucination
nodes.definition: A language model producing fluent, confident output that is factually false or fabricated.

nodes.name: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.definition: Studying a trained network's internal representations and circuits to explain how they cause its behavior.

nodes.name: Reward Hacking
nodes.definition: A model maximizing its training or evaluation signal in unintended ways that defeat the actual goal.

nodes.name: Research Taste
nodes.definition: The judgment to recognize which questions matter and which results are meaningful, built through repeated iteration.

nodes.name: Engineering Responsibility
nodes.definition: An engineer's awareness of where their work sits in a chain of tools and ends, and of the purposes it ultimately serves.
